reasons: The excerpt explicitly asks the audience to identify the top three fears potential customers may have about requesting the call to action.
The excerpt expressly makes overcoming each of the three identified objections the next part of the exercise.
Its dependency on first identifying the fears/objections follows the stated exercise sequence.
The excerpt specifically presents “no obligation,” eligibility/fit framing, and “apply for a discovery call” as low-pitch wording that can reduce the fear of being pitched.
For the stated e-commerce newsletter example, the excerpt identifies fear of spam and suggests saying that subscribers receive occasional, valuable tips on how to do X.
The action is directly supported: the excerpt says to tell people exactly what they will get.

However, the trigger improperly makes this advice contingent on explicitly identifying the fear of the unknown. The excerpt gives the fear-of-the-unknown statement as rationale, then gives the instruction generally; it does not state that identification as a prerequisite or trigger.
The excerpt directly instructs the audience to think through the exact process required to get the offer and whether that process creates objections.
The excerpt supports explaining the process on the lead-generation page when the process is long, in person, risky, or has serious objections.
The candidate changes the source's qualified recommendation (“you’re probably going to want to”) into an unqualified instruction (“Explain exactly”), omitting the stated uncertainty.
The excerpt explicitly says to use social proof not only to sell the business but also to sell the call to action, and frames this as important when visitors are being asked to trust the business.
The excerpt explicitly describes Exposure Ninja as taking the three listed objections about its free website and marketing review head-on.
The candidate appropriately presents this as an example and does not add an unprovided conversion result.
The excerpt expressly states that National Accident Helpline places another demonstration of credibility immediately next to the button users are expected to click.
This principle is stated verbatim in the excerpt: wherever people are being asked to trust the business, they should be given a reason to trust it.

Within the two-book Amazon example, the excerpt says most people choose the book with more reviews even though its average rating is worse, and attributes the choice to review volume rather than better reviews.
The excerpt gives the stated e-commerce email-signup example, including a 10% offer and a line that 42,000 other people receive the tips.
It expressly explains the intended effect as making a person feel safer because they are not the first person to take the action.
For a free-consultation offer, the excerpt provides the quoted wording and says the speaker's organization found it increases conversion rate.
The wording describes the next contact step, scheduling at the prospect's convenience, and the available consultation channels, which the excerpt says handles multiple objections.
The excerpt's free-site-survey/ADT discussion explicitly says that calling the offer a “free quote” removes the assumed objection that someone must come to the prospect's house.
The excerpt ends immediately after “Now, if you're a brand new,” so the candidate accurately records an unresolved, cut-off point without inferring its missing subject or recommendation.

omissions.description: The concrete Exposure Ninja method for differentiating a free review from generic free reviews is not represented: provide a personally recorded 15-minute video and a prioritized step-by-step plan.
omissions.quote: One of the team will actually do record you a 15-minute video showing you how to improve the volume of leads and sales through your website, and they'll put together a prioritized step-by-step plan that you can follow to do that.

omissions.description: The excerpt separately highlights positioning social proof around the call to action; the general social-proof candidate does not preserve this placement guidance.
omissions.quote: how to use social proof and how to position it around your call to action

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so surrounding context and the completed final recommendation are unavailable.
The excerpt refers to an earlier ADT example that is not included, limiting interpretation of that example's full setup.
Some wording appears to be an unedited spoken transcript, including apparent transcription errors, which may affect exact phrasing.

Claims that particular wording increases conversion rates and that users generally prefer higher review volume are asserted by the speaker, but no supporting measurements, study design, or underlying evidence are supplied in this excerpt.
